title: Fix build failure when frontend_path is set without prerendering
author: masenf
awaiting: no reviewer requested; blocked by its own failing CI, not by a human

failing_job_findings.check: unit-tests (windows-latest, 3.10/3.11/3.12/3.13/3.14) — all 5 windows jobs, same 3 tests
failing_job_findings.cause: Real bug introduced by this PR's own fix, not flaky/pre-existing. reflex/utils/build.py:292 does `frontend_path = PosixPath(frontend_path)` unconditionally. pathlib.PosixPath cannot be instantiated on Windows since Python 3.13+ (raises `pathlib.UnsupportedOperation: cannot instantiate 'PosixPath' on your system`), so all 3 of this PR's own new tests (test_build_relocates_static_output_without_prerendered_prefix_dir[/app], [/foo/bar], and test_build_merges_static_output_into_prerendered_prefix_dir) fail on every Windows unit-test job. Needs `pathlib.PurePosixPath` (for path manipulation only, works cross-platform) or platform-neutral handling instead of concrete PosixPath.

outstanding_asks.ask: Confidence 4/5, PR does NOT yet appear safe to merge: even after masenf's fix rejecting '..' segments, _normalize_paths still forces frontend_path to start with '/', and `static_dir / frontend_path` with an absolute right-hand path discards static_dir entirely (pathlib semantics) — so ordinary values like '/app' can still create/populate an output directory outside .web/build/client, not just deliberate traversal.

recent_comments.excerpt: The PR does not yet appear safe to merge because the existing output-containment issue remains unresolved ... static_dir / frontend_path discards static_dir.

Self-authored by masenf (MEMBER) — blocked purely by CI, not by a missing reviewer or human approval.

Real, reproducible CI failure caused by this PR's own code: reflex/utils/build.py:292 instantiates a concrete pathlib.PosixPath from a config string, which raises on Windows Python 3.13+. All 5 windows unit-test jobs fail on the 3 new tests this PR adds. This is a one-fix-away situation but the fix is not yet pushed.

greptile's most recent review (19:04, same head 04b3cefe that masenf's thread replies cite as 'fixed') says the path-containment concern is only partially fixed: rejecting '..' stops literal traversal, but joining an absolute frontend_path onto static_dir via pathlib's '/' operator silently discards static_dir for ordinary values like '/app', which is a second, still-open correctness issue in the same code region as the Windows CI failure.

Two review threads exist, both marked resolved by masenf's replies (citing the same 04b3cefe commit) — but the CI failure and greptile's newer finding suggest the fix is incomplete; do not treat 'resolved threads' as equivalent to 'actually fixed' here.
